rows.vgi.doc_llm: Extract acoustic and musical features from audio files or raw audio bytes directly in SQL. Scalars return per-file metadata (duration, sample_rate, channels) and signal/spectral/rhythmic features (tempo in BPM, rms_energy, zero_crossing_rate, spectral_centroid, spectral_bandwidth, mfcc as `DOUBLE[]`, and a heuristic estimated_key like 'C major'). Table functions return beat onset times (beats) and combined metadata (audio_info). Every function accepts either a `VARCHAR` filesystem path the worker opens, or a `BLOB` of raw audio bytes. Use it to index, filter, or cluster audio collections by their acoustic properties without leaving SQL.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# Audio Feature Extraction in SQL

![librosa logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/librosa/librosa/main/docs/img/librosa_logo_text.png)

Extract tempo, timbre, loudness, key, and rhythm descriptors from audio files and raw audio bytes directly in DuckDB SQL — no separate media pipeline required. The audio catalog turns music information retrieval (MIR) and digital signal processing primitives into ordinary SQL, so you can query, filter, and cluster large audio collections by their acoustic properties using nothing but SELECT.

This VGI worker is built for data engineers, music-tech developers, and ML practitioners who need audio descriptors without leaving the database. Every feature is computed by [librosa](https://librosa.org/), the de-facto standard Python library for audio and music analysis ([documentation](https://librosa.org/doc/latest/index.html), [source on GitHub](https://github.com/librosa/librosa)). Audio is decoded with libsndfile via [soundfile](https://python-soundfile.readthedocs.io/); WAV, FLAC, and OGG decode natively, while compressed formats such as MP3 and M4A use ffmpeg/audioread when available. DuckDB attaches the worker over Apache Arrow, streaming feature vectors back with zero-copy efficiency.

Every feature takes the audio two ways — a filesystem path the worker opens, or a blob of raw audio bytes — and undecodable or hostile input yields NULL (or no rows) rather than crashing. The features span a handful of families, from cheap per-file metadata and loudness levels through spectral-timbre descriptors and compact cepstral feature vectors to rhythm/beat tracking and a heuristic musical-key estimate; list the schema to browse them. Typical uses include building feature tables for audio search and recommendation, detecting tempo or key across a music library, filtering recordings by loudness or brightness, and generating embeddings for downstream clustering or classification — all in plain SQL.
